assets.capacity_text: About 12 percent of world trade in normal times
assets.note: Traffic still well below pre-2024 levels because of Red Sea attacks.

assets.name: Ceyhan
assets.capacity_text: About 2.4 million barrels/day combined pipeline capacity
assets.note: Outlet for Azeri and Iraqi crude.

assets.name: Novorossiysk
assets.capacity_text: About 2 million barrels/day including Caspian Pipeline Consortium
assets.note: Main Black Sea outlet for Russian and Kazakh crude. Drone strikes 2025.

assets.name: Primorsk
assets.note: Largest Russian Baltic port. Drone strikes 2025.

assets.name: Kozmino
assets.note: End of the Eastern Siberia-Pacific Ocean pipeline.

assets.name: Rotterdam
assets.note: Pricing centre for north-west European products.

assets.name: Trieste
assets.note: Feeds Austria, southern Germany and Czechia by the Transalpine Pipeline.

assets.name: Gdansk Naftoport
assets.note: Replaced Druzhba supply for Poland and eastern Germany.

assets.name: Corpus Christi port
assets.note: Largest United States crude export port.

assets.name: Louisiana Offshore Oil Port
assets.capacity_text: Only United States port able to fully load a very large crude carrier

assets.name: Cushing
assets.note: Delivery point for West Texas Intermediate futures. Inland.

assets.name: Vancouver Westridge
assets.note: End of Trans Mountain. Gave Canadian crude Pacific access in 2024.

assets.name: Acu
assets.capacity_text: About 25 percent of Brazilian crude exports

assets.name: Arzew port
assets.trade_role: Crude, LNG, liquefied petroleum gas export

assets.name: Walvis Bay
assets.note: Current logistics base for Orange Basin drilling.

assets.name: Luderitz
assets.capacity_text: Closest port to the Orange Basin
assets.note: Namport is developing an oil and gas supply base here. Shallow draft and limited land are the constraints.

assets.name: Mombasa port
assets.capacity_text: Main East African product import port

assets.name: Tanga
assets.capacity_text: End of the East African Crude Oil Pipeline
assets.note: Terminal under construction.

assets.name: Singapore
assets.capacity_text: Largest bunkering port in the world
assets.note: Asian pricing centre.

assets.name: Ningbo-Zhoushan
assets.capacity_text: Largest port in the world by tonnage

assets.name: Qingdao and Shandong ports
assets.note: Destination for most sanctioned Iranian, Russian and Venezuelan barrels.

assets.name: Duqm port
assets.note: Outside the Strait of Hormuz.

assets.name: Strait of Hormuz
assets.capacity_text: About 20 million barrels/day, plus about 20 percent of world LNG
assets.note: Most critical oil chokepoint. Bypass capacity is only about 2.6 million barrels/day. Closure threatened during the June 2025 Israel-Iran war.

assets.name: Strait of Malacca
assets.note: Busiest oil chokepoint by volume. Main route to China, Japan and South Korea.

assets.name: Suez Canal and SUMED
assets.capacity_text: About 9 million barrels/day in normal times
assets.note: Flows well below normal since Houthi attacks began in late 2023.

assets.name: Bab el-Mandeb
assets.capacity_text: About 4 million barrels/day currently, half of pre-2024
assets.note: Red Sea gateway. Most Western-linked tankers and nearly all LNG carriers still divert round the Cape.

assets.name: Turkish Straits
assets.note: Outlet for Russian and Kazakh Black Sea crude.

assets.name: Danish Straits
assets.note: Outlet for Russian Baltic crude. Shadow fleet scrutiny rising.

assets.name: Panama Canal
assets.capacity_text: About 2 million barrels/day, mostly products and liquefied petroleum gas
assets.note: Drought restrictions in 2023-24 pushed United States LNG to the Cape route. Many LNG carriers still avoid it.

assets.name: Cape of Good Hope
assets.capacity_text: About 9 million barrels/day, up sharply since 2024
assets.note: The diversion route when the Red Sea is unsafe. Adds 10 to 14 days to Asia-Europe voyages.

assets.name: Hoegh Gandria (Egypt, incoming)
assets.capacity_text: Hoegh Gandria, about 1 billion cubic feet/day peak
assets.note: Ten-year deployment agreed. Replaces short-term units and signals Egypt expects to import for a decade.
assets.charter_note: Ten-year time charter signed May 2025. Deployment at Sumed port scheduled for late 2026. Replaces Hoegh Galleon.

assets.name: Khor Al Zubair
assets.operator: Iraq Ministry of Electricity / Excelerate Energy
assets.note: Definitive agreement signed October 2025. Start-up slipped from 2026 to 2027 because of the regional conflict. Dredging under way in August 2026.
assets.charter_note: Five years renewable, with a minimum contracted offtake. Excelerate also supplies the LNG.
assets.source: Excelerate Energy, Iraqi News, Dredging Today

assets.name: Nador West Med
assets.note: Tender launched 2025. Would end reliance on reverse flow through Spain.
assets.charter_note: Tender stage.

assets.name: Jebel Ali
assets.note: Seasonal summer imports.
assets.charter_note: Extended several times. Current end date not known.

assets.name: Aliaga (Etki)
assets.charter_note: Not known.

assets.name: Acu (GNA)
assets.note: Feeds 3 gigawatts of gas-fired power at the port.
assets.charter_note: Twenty-three years from 2021.

assets.name: Bahia
assets.charter_note: Ten years from 2024.

assets.name: Lampung
assets.charter_note: Twenty years from 2014.

assets.name: West Java (Jakarta Bay)
assets.note: First FSRU in Asia, 2012.
assets.charter_note: Extended past the original 2022 end. Current end date not known.

assets.name: Kerawalapitiya
assets.note: Repeatedly re-tendered.
assets.charter_note: No vessel contracted.

assets.name: Taranaki
assets.note: Announced 2025 in response to declining domestic gas.
assets.charter_note: No vessel contracted.

assets.name: Beni Suef
assets.note: One of three Siemens mega-plants. Egypt needs roughly 60 billion cubic metres/year and produces well under that. The gap is filled by Israeli pipeline gas and LNG.

assets.name: Burullus
assets.note: Summer peak drives the LNG buying season.

assets.name: Samra and central Jordan plants
assets.note: About 85 percent of Jordanian power is gas-fired. Exposed whenever Israeli flows are cut.

assets.name: Deir Ammar and Zahrani
assets.note: Built for gas, never supplied. Floating terminal plans shelved several times. Supply through the Arab Gas Pipeline is the cheaper fix.

assets.name: Deir Ali and Syrian grid
assets.note: Reconstruction demand. Qatar-funded gas supply and 5 gigawatts of new plants agreed with a Turkish-Qatari-American group.

assets.name: Vasilikos power station
assets.operator: Fuel oil until the floating terminal starts
assets.note: Highest power prices in the European Union while the plant waits for gas.

assets.name: Basra and southern Iraq plants
assets.operator: Iranian pipeline gas, flared gas capture
assets.note: United States waiver for Iranian supply ended in 2025. Drives the floating terminal at Khor Al Zubair.

assets.name: Tahaddart and Ain Beni Mathar
assets.operator: LNG landed in Spain, reverse flow
assets.note: New Al Wahda gas plants planned. Demand case for the Nador terminal.

assets.name: Tunisian grid
assets.note: Over 95 percent gas-fired. Wholly dependent on Algeria.

assets.name: Cap des Biches and Dakar plants
assets.operator: Heavy fuel oil and LNG now. Domestic gas later
assets.note: West African Energy 366 megawatt combined-cycle plant started 2025. State plan converts the fleet to gas. Bridge period needs imported LNG.

assets.name: Abidjan plants (Azito, CIPREL, Atinkou)
assets.note: Earlier LNG import project shelved after the Baleine discovery.

assets.name: Tema and Takoradi enclaves
assets.operator: Domestic gas and West African Gas Pipeline
assets.note: Persistent gas payment arrears. Tema LNG idle beside it.

assets.name: Maria Gleta
assets.note: Unreliable Nigerian supply has kept a floating import option alive.

assets.name: Nigerian grid (Egbin, Azura and others)
assets.capacity_text: About 12 gigawatts installed, under half available
assets.note: Gas shortfalls and debts to suppliers strand capacity.

assets.name: Kudu and southern Namibia
assets.note: Namibia imports most of its power from South Africa.

assets.name: Richards Bay combined cycle
assets.note: Environmental approval overturned in court, then reinstated on appeal. Anchor demand for the Richards Bay terminal.

assets.name: Ankerlig and Gourikwa
assets.note: Burning diesel as peakers. Conversion needs an import terminal in the Western Cape.

assets.name: Gauteng industrial gas market
assets.note: Supply from Mozambique declines from about 2028. Known locally as the gas cliff. Industrial users, not power.

assets.name: Temane
assets.note: Commissioning. Largest new plant in Mozambique since independence.

assets.name: Kinyerezi, Dar es Salaam
assets.operator: Domestic Songo Songo and Mnazi Bay gas

assets.name: Mombasa LNG-to-power
assets.note: Floated repeatedly. Geothermal keeps crowding it out.

assets.name: Algerian domestic demand
assets.note: Domestic use now rivals export volume. The main long-term threat to Algerian supply to Europe.

assets.name: Libyan grid
assets.note: Summer shortages cut Greenstream exports to Italy.

assets.name: Sonker liquid bulk terminal, Ain Sokhna
assets.capacity_text: 100,000 cubic metres gasoil and 150,000 cubic metres LPG storage, plus FSRU berths
assets.operator: Sonker Bunkering Company (Egyptian Amiral Petroleum Services 51 percent; Misr Petroleum 15; Suez Canal Economic Zone authority 12; Ministry of Finance 12; Petroleum Cooperative 10)
assets.trade_role: LPG, gasoil and LNG import; ammonia export
assets.note: Basin 3 of Sokhna Port, under an agreement with DP World Sokhna. Completed 2020. Hosts the berths where Egypt's floating LNG terminals dock. 25-year supply point agreement with EGPC. Gasoil pipeline of 37.5 kilometres to the national grid. Original project cost about 417 million dollars; a refinancing of up to 355 million dollars was disclosed in 2022 and is still listed as pending.
assets.source: International Finance Corporation project disclosures 36828 and 44905; EBRD

assets.name: Ain Sokhna onshore LNG terminal (tender)
assets.capacity_text: About 1 billion cubic feet/day initially, with floating storage of up to 290,000 cubic metres
assets.note: Egypt's first permanent regasification terminal. Three bidders reported in August 2026: BGN of Turkey, UCC Holding of Qatar and a local player. Cost, award date and construction timing not disclosed. Would reduce reliance on leased floating units.

routes.name: Druzhba
routes.note: Northern branch to Poland and Germany carries only Kazakh crude now. Southern branch to Hungary and Slovakia still carries Russian crude, hit repeatedly by Ukrainian strikes in 2025.

routes.name: Eastern Siberia-Pacific Ocean
routes.note: Main Russian route to Asia. Spur to Daqing supplies China directly.

routes.name: Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan
routes.capacity_text: 1.2 million barrels/day design, runs about half
routes.note: Carries Azeri crude, plus some Kazakh and Turkmen volumes.

routes.name: Caspian Pipeline Consortium
routes.note: Carries over 80 percent of Kazakh exports across Russia. Pump stations hit by drones in 2025.

routes.name: Kirkuk-Ceyhan
routes.note: Restarted September 2025 after a two and a half year shutdown. Volumes still modest.

routes.name: East-West Pipeline (Petroline)
routes.note: Saudi bypass of the Strait of Hormuz.

routes.name: Habshan-Fujairah
routes.note: Abu Dhabi bypass of the Strait of Hormuz.

routes.name: SUMED
routes.note: Links Red Sea to Mediterranean for tankers too large for the Suez Canal.

routes.name: Goreh-Jask
routes.capacity_text: About 1 million barrels/day design, lightly used
routes.note: Iranian bypass of the Strait of Hormuz.

routes.name: Basra-Aqaba
routes.note: Proposed for over a decade. No financing.

routes.name: Keystone
routes.note: Canadian heavy crude to Cushing and the Gulf Coast. Keystone XL extension cancelled 2021.

routes.name: Enbridge Mainline
routes.note: Largest crude system in North America.

routes.name: Trans Mountain
routes.note: Expansion opened May 2024. Only Canadian crude line to the Pacific.

routes.name: Colonial (refined products)
routes.note: Largest United States products line. Gulf Coast to New York Harbor.

routes.name: East African Crude Oil Pipeline
routes.note: Longest heated crude pipeline in the world. Construction well advanced. First oil targeted 2026 - verify.

routes.name: Niger-Benin
routes.note: China-built. Flow repeatedly interrupted by Niger-Benin border dispute.

routes.name: Kazakhstan-China
routes.note: Also carries Russian crude in transit.

routes.name: Myanmar-China oil and gas
routes.capacity_text: About 440 thousand barrels/day oil, 12 billion cubic metres/year gas
routes.note: Lets Gulf crude reach Yunnan without passing the Strait of Malacca.

routes.name: Baltic Pipeline System
routes.note: Feeds Primorsk and Ust-Luga.

routes.name: Transalpine Pipeline
routes.note: Supplies Austria, Bavaria and all of Czechia since 2025.

routes.name: Vaca Muerta Oil Sur
routes.note: Largest private infrastructure project in Argentina. Opens deepwater Atlantic export.

routes.name: Nord Stream 1 and 2
routes.note: Three of four strings destroyed September 2022. No flow.

routes.name: Yamal-Europe
routes.note: Idle for Russian gas since 2022. Polish section runs in reverse.

routes.name: Ukraine transit corridor
routes.note: Transit contract expired 1 January 2025. No Russian flow.

routes.name: TurkStream
routes.note: Last Russian pipeline route into Europe.

routes.name: Power of Siberia
routes.note: At full contracted flow since late 2024.

routes.name: Power of Siberia 2
routes.note: Legally binding memorandum signed September 2025. Price and financing still open.

routes.name: Central Asia-China
routes.note: Three parallel lines. Fourth line (Line D) stalled.

routes.name: West-East Gas Pipelines
routes.capacity_text: Over 77 billion cubic metres/year across lines
routes.note: Backbone of the Chinese gas grid.

routes.name: Southern Gas Corridor (SCP, TANAP, TAP)
routes.capacity_text: About 16 billion cubic metres/year onward to Europe
routes.note: Azeri gas to Turkey, Greece and Italy.

routes.name: Langeled
routes.note: Norway to the United Kingdom.

routes.name: Europipe system
routes.note: Norway to Germany.

routes.name: Baltic Pipe
routes.note: Norwegian gas to Poland through Denmark.

routes.name: TransMed
routes.note: Algeria to Italy through Tunisia. Algeria is now the largest pipeline supplier to Italy.

routes.name: Medgaz
routes.note: Algeria direct to Spain.

routes.name: Maghreb-Europe
routes.note: Algeria stopped supply in 2021. Runs in reverse to feed Morocco from Spain.

routes.name: Greenstream
routes.capacity_text: About 11 billion cubic metres/year design, runs far lower
routes.note: Libya to Sicily.

routes.name: Arab Gas Pipeline
routes.note: Now carries Israeli gas into Jordan and Egypt, and Azerbaijani-sourced gas toward Syria.

routes.name: East Mediterranean Gas (Ashkelon-Arish)
routes.capacity_text: About 7 billion cubic metres/year, being expanded
routes.note: Israeli exports to Egypt. Flows cut during conflict peaks in 2025.

routes.name: EastMed
routes.note: Israel-Cyprus-Greece. Commercially stalled.

routes.name: West African Gas Pipeline
routes.note: Nigerian gas to Benin, Togo and Ghana.

routes.name: Nigeria-Morocco (African Atlantic)
routes.note: Thirteen-country offshore route. Feasibility done. Financing not secured.

routes.name: Trans-Saharan
routes.note: Nigeria-Niger-Algeria. Rival to the Atlantic route.

routes.name: Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano
routes.note: Nigerian domestic backbone. First leg of any Trans-Saharan line.

routes.name: Dolphin
routes.note: Qatar to the United Arab Emirates and Oman.

routes.name: Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India
routes.note: Afghan section started in 2024-25. Onward financing absent.

routes.name: Bolivia-Brazil
routes.note: Bolivian supply collapsing. Being repurposed to carry Argentine gas north.

routes.name: Perito Moreno (Vaca Muerta gas)
routes.note: Formerly Nestor Kirchner. Ended Argentine winter LNG dependence.

routes.name: Transco
routes.note: Largest United States gas system by volume.

routes.name: Permian to Gulf Coast lines
routes.note: Matterhorn Express added 2024. More lines under construction to feed LNG.

routes.name: Coastal GasLink
routes.note: Feeds LNG Canada.

routes.name: Gulf to Asia (crude)
routes.note: Largest crude trade lane. Very large crude carriers through Hormuz and Malacca to China, India, Japan and South Korea.

routes.name: Gulf to Europe via Suez (crude)
routes.note: Many operators still avoid the Red Sea.

routes.name: Gulf to Europe via the Cape (diversion)
routes.note: Used while Red Sea risk persists.

routes.name: West Africa to Europe (crude)
routes.note: Nigerian and Angolan grades. Less Nigerian crude leaves now that Dangote runs it at home.

routes.name: West Africa to Asia (crude)
routes.note: Angolan crude to China, Nigerian to India.

routes.name: United States Gulf to Europe (crude)
routes.note: United States crude became the largest single supply to Europe after 2022.

routes.name: Brazil and Guyana to Asia (crude)
routes.note: Fastest-growing long-haul crude lane.

routes.name: Russia Baltic to India and China (shadow fleet)
routes.note: Sanctioned trade. Mostly older tankers with opaque ownership. Target of new United States sanctions on Rosneft and Lukoil in October 2025.

routes.name: Black Sea to Mediterranean (crude)
routes.note: Russian and Kazakh crude through the Turkish Straits.

routes.name: Kozmino to north China (crude)
routes.note: Short-haul sanctioned trade.

routes.name: Vancouver to Asia (crude)
routes.note: New since Trans Mountain expansion.

routes.name: Qatar to Asia (LNG)
routes.note: Largest LNG lane.

routes.name: Qatar to Europe via the Cape (LNG)
routes.note: LNG carriers have almost entirely avoided the Red Sea since January 2024.

routes.name: United States Gulf to Europe (LNG)
routes.note: United States is the largest LNG exporter and the largest supplier to Europe.

routes.name: United States Gulf to Asia via Panama (LNG)
routes.note: Fastest route to Japan and South Korea when slots are available.

routes.name: Yamal to Europe (LNG)
routes.capacity_text: About 17 million tonnes/year, to be banned
routes.note: European Union ban on Russian LNG phases in from 2026 for short-term contracts and January 2027 for long-term.

routes.name: Northern Sea Route to Asia (LNG, seasonal)
routes.note: Used by Yamal and sanctioned Arctic LNG 2 cargoes to reach China.

routes.name: West Africa to Europe (LNG)
routes.note: Nigeria, Angola, Equatorial Guinea, Senegal-Mauritania.

routes.name: Canada west coast to Asia (LNG)
routes.note: Opened mid-2025. About 10 days to Japan.

routes.name: India to Europe (diesel, jet)
routes.note: European Union ban on products refined from Russian crude takes effect in 2026.

routes.name: Gulf to East Africa (products)
routes.capacity_text: Main supply for Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique

routes.name: Europe to West Africa (gasoline)
routes.note: Dangote is displacing European gasoline exports to Nigeria.

routes.name: United States Gulf to Latin America (products)
routes.note: Mexico and Brazil are the largest buyers.
